interest: Shows public inquiries about Adm. Yamamoto's 1943 death, with State citing only Tokyo radio despite secret US codebreaking.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.321, covering commissioned officers of the Japanese Navy between November 1940 and May 1943) comprises two main components: a 1940 cross-reference sheet noting career details of Admiral Ryozo Nakamura from an Embassy Tokyo telegram, and a May 1943 constituent correspondence exchange initiated by Wisconsin resident George P. Kornely. Forwarded by Senator Alexander Wiley to Secretary of State Cordell Hull, Kornely's inquiry sought information regarding the death and funeral of Admiral Isoroku Yamamoto. The Department of State, via Laurence E. Salisbury of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, replied with details derived exclusively from monitored Tokyo radio broadcasts reporting Yamamoto's death in an airplane, the honors bestowed by the Emperor, the transport of his ashes to Tokyo for a state funeral alongside Fleet Admiral Togo, and the appointment of Admiral Mineichi Koga as his successor.
